We will use the fact that

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r.
$$

We're given the value of the first integral, so we only need to work out the second.

The path ${C}_{2}$ is the vertical line segment from $B$ to $D.$ It can be parametrized as

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{2}(t) & =b+t(d-b) \\  & =⟨-1,2⟩+t(⟨-1,0⟩-⟨-1,2⟩) \\  & =⟨-1,2-2t⟩ \\  & =-\,i+(2-2t)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $0<t<1.$ Along this segment, we have $x=-1$ and $y=2-2t.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F({r}_{2}(t)) & =(x-y)\,i+(y-x)\,j \\  & =(-1-(2-2t))\,i+(2-2t-(-1))\,j \\  & =(-3+2t)\,i+(3-2t)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the derivative, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{2}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-1)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2-2t)j \\  & =-2\,j\end{aligned}
$$

We can now compute the dot product:

$$
\begin{aligned}F({r}_{2}(t))\cdot {r}_{2}^{′}(t) & =((-3+2t)\,i+(3-2t)\,j)\cdot (-2\,j) \\  & =(3-2t)\cdot (-2) \\  & =4t-6\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can evaluate the integral, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r \\  & =-\frac{7}{2}+{\int }_{0}^{1}F({r}_{2}(t))\cdot {r}_{2}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-\frac{7}{2}+{\int }_{0}^{1}(4t-6)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-\frac{7}{2}+[2{t}^{2}-6t]_{0}^{1} \\  & =-\frac{7}{2}+[2({1}^{2})-6(1)-0] \\  & =-\frac{7}{2}-4 \\  & =-\frac{15}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
